ΕΙΔΟΣ Α.
Argumentum.
QVum Delij petiissent à Pindaro, vt Apollini car-
men componeret, sub idem tempus Herodoti vi-
ctoria denuntiata est, petitumque à Pindaro vt hymnum
scriberet. Priori ergo argumento omisso, convertit se ad
concedendum Herodoti laudes. Quare exordium αὐξω-
μίλῳ[?] habet, excusat enim sese apud Delios, cur prius illi
laudandus fuerit Herodotus, quàm Apollo Delius. Hinc
ingressus encomium, patriam laudat à victoriarum multitu-
dine, clara origine, ab Hercule cociue. Inde ipsum Hero-
dotum à præsenti victoria, Castori & Iolao eum conferes,
per digressiunculam horum claras victorias celebrat, re-
ditum inde instituit ad Herodoti causam, ac à patre Aso-
pedoro laudat: huius fortuna breuiter describit, ex The-
bis exilium in Orchomenum, & quomodo feliciter de-
mum Thebis sit restitutus. A consequenti ostendit etiam
deberi Herodoto laudes, quòd & laboribus & impensis
in virtutis studio nunquam pepercerit: hoc ad poetas spe-
ctare, vt bonos celebrent. Utiles autem fuisse labores &
sumptus Herodoti ostendit multis victoriis, quas non
omnes enumerat, quod interdum utilius sit, quædam au-
ditoris iudicio & opinioni relinquere. Hinc sequitur epi-
logus comprecatione constans, quo à diis petit vt eadem
felicitate & in Pythiis & Olympiis vincat, quemad. ha-
ctenus in aliis certaminibus victor abiit. Extrema clausula
in auaros composita est vt eo liberaliorem habeat Hero-
dotum.
PARTES igitur tres sunt, exordium excusatione offi-
cij sui constans, quod Delios attinet: complectitur e-
tiam propositionem, se & patriæ & Delijs satisfactu-

page.notes: Large initial Q of "QVum" is a woodcut-style initial, joined to the word. The Greek word after "Quare exordium" is hard to read; the letters given are a best reading and are marked [?]. The Greek phrase "ἐγκωμιαστικὸν λόγον" is also marked [?]. "ΕΙΔΟΣ Α." is a Greek heading in capitals; the letter A is taken as printed. Hyphenated line-end words kept with their printed hyphens. "quemad." is printed with a stop as an abbreviation and kept. The catchword "tum" completes "Herodotum".
